angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 626,130 km at 217.27 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 4.6026 +/- 0.0893 mas (same row, RUWE 6.84): 217.27 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.9 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Anderson et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...604A.110A/abstract): 626,130 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.89 +/- 0.09 solar masses from Anderson et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...604A.110A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5070 +/- 130 K from Anderson et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...604A.110A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Anderson et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...604A.110A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-105.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.479, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
